text.L1: A magnet does not attract every metal. We must test each material.
text.L2: Magnets attract iron, nickel, cobalt, and steels that contain iron.
text.L3: Aluminium, copper and brass are metals, but they are not attracted. Plastic, wood, paper, rubber and glass are not attracted either.
text.L4: So a shiny or metal-looking object is not automatically magnetic.
text.L5: In our example, test the iron tawa, foil, steel spoon and plastic lid one at a time.
text.L6: Record each result, then group the objects as attracted or not attracted.
text.L7: A magnet can act through paper, cloth, glass and water. It can even pull a paper clip through a glass of water.
text.L8: Two steel spoons can behave differently, so testing is the reliable way to sort materials.

guard.firstDraft: Ab ek naya object sochiye; uska magnet ke paas reaction observe karke record karenge. Paani ke glass ke andar neeche ek paper clip padi hai. Guess kariye: kya bahar se tez magnet ghuma kar, paani ko chhuiye-e bina, clip ko glass ki deewar ke saath upar la sakte ho?

turns.childText: ek minute ruko, bathroom jaana hai
turns.teacherReply: Theek hai, Zoya. Break lijiye; lesson yahin rukega. Wapas aakar hum paper clip wale magnet test ko ek-ek step mein karenge.

move.shape: they asked for a short break: agree warmly; the lesson waits right here for them; one line for when they are back; no question now; address them with aap forms only (aap, aapka, aapne; verbs -iye / -enge), never tum or tu

move.shape: two parts — first: they are back after a moment away: welcome them back in two or three words, no goodbye and no fuss; carry on; second: the question on the card, as written, in their language; then wait; no verdict on their reply: neither praise nor 'wrong'; address them with aap forms only (aap, aapka, aapne; verbs -iye / -enge), never tum or tu
